author: Jashayla Pettigrew
title: New Elephants Delicatessen owners to replace Northwest Portland location - NewsBreak
text:
By Jashayla Pettigrew ,
1 days ago PORTLAND, Ore. ( KOIN ) — Nearly seven months after a fire destroyed a Northwest Portland deli , new ownership is working to bring another location to the area.
Elephants Delicatessen revealed on Wednesday that it expects to start operations on 13 NW 23rd Place in the Uptown Shopping Center early next year. It will be the first location opened under the leadership of The Ground, a farm and hospitality company based in Carlton.
Salt & Straw vs. Ruby Jewel: Portland ice cream brands feud over Tacolate agreement The Ground co-founder Frank Foti will step in as the CEO of Elephants Delicatessen, according to the announcement. He has signed a definitive agreement to take over the shares of the deli’s majority stakeholder, Henry Hillman — who has led the company for more than four years as it expanded and partnered with more than 40 other businesses, like New Seasons and Williams-Sonoma.
Crews battled a fire at the flagship Elephants Delicatessen location in Northwest Portland (PF&R) “Henry’s foresight and investment have produced a great foundation from which The Ground can expand Elephants’ geographical reach and add regenerative offerings to the amazing options already available,” Foti said in a statement. “The humble and caring culture that exists at Elephants and The Ground are a beautiful fit, and the chance to serve all of Oregon and SW Washington is an exciting prospect for us all.”
Elephants’ former CEO Martin McClanan will remain president of the deli, in addition to serving as a leader of The Ground.
[sailthru_widget name="Sailthru Widget Block" sailthru_list="Daily News" title="KOIN Morning Digest"] The transition follows the shutdown of Elephants’ flagship location on Northwest 22nd Avenue that first opened in 2004. The restaurant, located just blocks away from where the new spot will debut next year, was damaged by a fire earlier in March.
Portland Fire & Rescue responded to the blaze at the deli around 1:40 a.m. on Tuesday, March 10.
Crews were unable to battle it from the inside due to the heavy fire and structural issues, but they later extinguished it by cutting holes through the roof and using an aerial nozzle to battle the flames from above — though the damage was still enough to spark the closure of the restaurant.
Fire officials identified Catherine Stough as a suspect in the incident the following day. The 56-year-old woman was arrested for second-degree criminal mischief and reckless burning.
‘Honor of my life to coach the Ducks’: Oregon men’s basketball head coach Dana Altman retiring Stough, who was identified as homeless , told investigators the fire was merely an accident and she was attempting to stay warm. On the night of the blaze, she used "an open flame torch as a light source to view into garbage cans when the flame unintentionally ignited a combustible material inside,” according to PF&R.
She was sentenced to six months in jail later in May, after changing her plea to guilty.
